ssj_ui_content.visioning_description: The Visioning phase is a reflective period where teachers explore their purpose, school vision, and alignment with Wildflower’s principles. Teachers document their vision in a Wildflower Visioning Album, which is shared with a group of network and community members for advice. While every team moves at their own pace, this phase typically takes one to two months, allowing time for deep reflection and growth. Many teachers share that this phase provides a helpful framework for clarifying their purpose, school vision and timeline, all of which are foundational for a successful school plan.
ssj_ui_content.planning_description: In the Planning phase, your team will refine the vision, budget, and timeline for the school and begin to form key elements of the business. These plans are recorded in a Wildflower Planning Album and are shared with the same team of advice givers for feedback. The Planning phase culminates with a decision to sign the membership agreement with Wildflower. While timelines vary greatly, many teams spend four to six months in the Planning phase and ideally complete the Planning phase seven to nine months before they intend to open the school.
ssj_ui_content.startup_description: The Startup phase is active and involves the operationalization of your school plans. During this phase, most schools will form as a non-profit organization, lease and renovate a facility, engage their community, fundraise, and enroll families. While this phase can sometimes take 6 to 9 months, timelines are likely to be impacted by the availability of facilities, access to capital, renovations, and licensing. Because of this, Wildflower recommends scheduling regular timeline check-ins and remaining flexible and adaptive as your plans shift.

ways_to_work_together.revisit_your_learning_and_growth_plan: Revisit your learning and growth plan
ways_to_work_together.revisit_your_learning_and_growth_plan_de: From time to time, you may want to revisit the Learning and Growth plan in your Visioning album and use it to guide you towards additional learning opportunities. If you would like to make a new Learning and Growth Plan, you can use this link to access the 'Emerging Teacher Leader Self-Awareness Reflective Guide' and accompanying presentation.
ways_to_work_together.learn_about_wildflower_ways_of_working: Learn about Wildflower Ways of Working
ways_to_work_together.learn_about_wildflower_ways_of_working_d: This resource provides six, self-guided learning modules on Wildflower Ways of Working. The six modules include; An Introduction to Self-Management and Domination Culture; The Advice Process; Roles & Responsibilities; Conflict Resolution; Radical Transparency; and Integration.
ways_to_work_together.learn_about_liberatory_leadership_descri: These sessions explore our collective vision for what ‘Liberatory Montessori’ means at Wildflower and how we support our ongoing development in service of our shared purpose for liberation in our schools and communities.
ways_to_work_together.enroll_in_equity_training_description: Wildflower Teacher Leaders and Foundation partners commit to a lifelong journey of personal racial identity development, critical consciousness, and anti-bias anti-racist action (commonly referred to as ABAR). You can use this list of vetted equity trainings to support you along your learning journey.
ways_to_work_together.identify_a_teacher_leader_partner_descri: Finding a Teacher Leader partner can be a daunting task, but there are ways to spread the word and activate your network. This resource provides reflection prompts, templates and framing to help you chart a path towards finding a supportive partnership.
ways_to_work_together.engage_a_growth_and_connectedness_coach: Engage a Growth and Connectedness Coach
ways_to_work_together.engage_a_growth_and_connectedness_coach_: Once you have identified a partner, Wildflower highly recommends investing in your partnership by engaging a Growth & Connectedness coach. Growth & Connectedness coaches typically focus on leadership, identity, and teamwork development. If you have questions about how to access coaching, please contact your Operations Guide.
ways_to_work_together.engage_an_equity_or_abar_coach: Engage an Equity or ABAR Coach
ways_to_work_together.engage_an_equity_or_abar_coach_descripti: In addition to attending equity trainings, some Teacher Leaders engage an equity or ABAR coach to support their ongoing racial-identity work. This work is critical to creating an intentionally anti-racist, anti-bias school community.
ways_to_work_together.attend_wildflower_community_events_descr: As an Emerging Teacher Leader you can begin attending Wildflower events and offerings. You can use this calendar to identify upcoming opportunities. When in doubt, you can also reach out to your Operations Guide to identify upcoming opportunities.
ways_to_work_together.learn_about_wildflower_school_pods_descr: Pods are small groupings of 5 - 7 schools that provide mutual support, accountability and community for one another. Read this first-hand account from a Teacher Leader about her experience of a Pod in a decentralized network. Schools typically join a Pod once they have signed a Membership Agreement with Wildflower, however it is never too early to begin learning about pods or even observe a pod meeting. To get connected, please contact your Operations Guide.
